discovery.title: AI’s progress on theoretical problems is accelerating across sciences
discovery.summary: A study discussed by WIRED reports that top AI models’ success on selected theoretical problems across several fields rose from about 2% in mid-2024 to about 35% in mid-2026. This measures performance on a set of problems, not general scientific ability or independent discovery.
discovery.why_it_matters: If AI tools become more capable across disciplines, research workflows, training and the role of human verification may all change.

discovery.title: Chinese pottery points to Great Zimbabwe’s far-reaching trade
discovery.summary: A report on archaeological work at Great Zimbabwe describes Chinese pottery fragments at the medieval African city, adding evidence of connections spanning long distances. The find offers a vivid way to explore trade networks and the sophistication of precolonial African societies.
discovery.why_it_matters: Material evidence of long-distance exchange can reshape how people understand medieval African economies and global connections.

discovery.title: Webb may have caught a distant supernova just days after its explosion
discovery.summary: Researchers reported a possible supernova in a galaxy seen as it was about 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang. Observations suggest it may have been detected only days after the explosion, but the event and its interpretation remain under study.
discovery.why_it_matters: Catching a distant stellar explosion early could help scientists investigate how massive stars lived and died in the young universe.

discovery.title: A famous impact crater may be far younger than scientists thought
discovery.summary: New dating places an American impact crater roughly 100 million years younger than previous estimates, near a major Late Devonian extinction event. The timing raises a possible connection, but does not show that the impact caused the extinction.
discovery.why_it_matters: Revised dates can change how scientists investigate links between extraterrestrial impacts and major changes in life on Earth.

discovery.title: A large asteroid appears to spin once in just over four minutes
discovery.summary: A report on Vera C. Rubin Observatory data describes an asteroid about 2.5 kilometers across rotating in a little over four minutes, making it an unusually large ultra-fast rotator. The discovery also illustrates how new survey methods can revise measurements from telescope observations.
discovery.why_it_matters: Asteroid spin can reveal clues about internal strength and structure, while better surveys improve our picture of small bodies in the solar system.
